name: Tan Son Nhut
summary: The base Larry remembers as home, and as his company headquarters: the place he radioed from Núi Bà Đen on the day of the "450 civilians" accusation, and where a medic told him he had yellow jaundice at the end of his tour. In his own spelling it is "Ton Son Nuht"; the name matches Tân Sơn Nhứt, the air base beside Saigon, though no document yet places him there. From the photographs he has given it a layout: his hooch, T 123; the radio van where he worked, often the night shift alone; the EM Club, "About 50 yards from my hooch"; the flight line, "probably 3 blocks away"; a road near the airport end, "We had to walk down this road to get a Taxi," with "a machine gun nest at the end of the road" and an orphanage near it. His company area had "maybe 10 hooches and a big BBQ'ing area with steaks. 24 hours a day you could get a steak…" And: "I felt safer on the mountain that I did at Ton Son Nhut."
researchNotes: Provenance of the name: "Ton Son Nuht" is the spelling marked as his in his 2026-08-13 comments (giscus-stories-c18006791, -c18006833); "Thom Son Nuht" was his son's earlier transcription of the name as Larry says it aloud; the other forms are his son's renderings of the sound, and the 2026-08-23 comment itself says "I might be misspelling this." The identification with Tân Sơn Nhứt stays plausible on one witness and no documentary support, and no coordinates are set until it is settled. Each placement of a single frame here (VN-0001 to VN-0003, VN-0007, VN-0008, VN-0011 to VN-0017, VN-0019, VN-0020, VN-0024, VN-0027, VN-0030 to VN-0034, VN-0055, VN-0067, VN-0070, VN-0151, VN-0152) is his, and is rated as such on the photograph; at VN-0026 he was "Not sure of the location" and reasoned it "Had to be in our company area." He also puts the AR-15 of VN-0019 here as "one of the first one's in Vietnam", which fits the 1964 issue of the rifle to Army aviation and advisory units before the M16 became general; Sarge the monkey was photographed in the barracks (VN-0152). 2026-09-12: he drew the flight line from memory (VD-0004); the inscriptions on that sheet not yet read by him stay in research/drawings/README.md. The analysis of which units stood on this base, which stood in this field until 2026-09-14, was moved to research/places/records-cleanup-2026-09-14.md after research/site-audit-2026-09-14.md: unit designations stay out of records while his unit is an open cold question (ledger #2). None of this moves the identification, which still rests on the name. 2026-09-15: "Tân Sơn Nhứt (the air base the name matches)" and "Tan Son Nhut" were taken out of the rendered alternate names when this page came back, on his son's decision: the identification is plausible, not confirmed, and which base was home is still to be asked (breakfast-questions, tier 2). The name stays his spelling until a document settles it. 2026-09-15, on his son's decision (no spelling notes on public pages): the rendered alternate names were trimmed; removed from display, kept here: "Thom Son Nuht (earlier family transcription)"; "Ton Son Nhut (as typed at the photographs, 2026-09-12)"; "Ton Suhn Nhut / Tah Suhn Nhut (his son's transcriptions, 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-05)"; "Thon Sohn Nuht (his son's transcription, 2026-08-23)". The page now uses the standard spelling, Tan Son Nhut, in place of "“Ton Son Nuht” (Larry’s own spelling)". The identification is still rated plausible on the name alone; his spellings stay in his recollections as given, and "Ton Son Nuht" remains the spelling marked as his (2026-08-13). This supersedes the same-day note above keeping the page name as his spelling. 2026-09-15, standard public place names (his son's rule, CLAUDE.md "Place names"): Tân Sơn Nhứt removed from the alternate names; it shows as the vietnameseName line.
